name: Raw Water Intake Station & Intake Tower
description: Submerged river intake structure with coarse/fine bar screens, trash racks, and submerged intake conduits to pull raw water from natural sources into the treatment plant.
what: A heavy reinforced concrete civil structure submerged or positioned at riverbank edge designed to withdraw raw surface water while screening floating debris and aquatic organisms.
why: Protects downstream pumping equipment and treatment processes from large physical obstructions, logs, silt deposits, and trash while ensuring continuous water withdrawal.
how: Raw river water flows by gravity through coarse bar racks into concrete intake shafts, where debris is mechanically raked off before water enters low-lift pump suction conduits.
engineeringPurpose: Continuous, regulated abstraction of surface water while excluding debris and maintaining hydraulic intake velocity below 0.15 m/s to protect aquatic species.

components.how: Conveys raw water by gravity head differential.

name: Low-Lift Raw Water Pumping Station
description: High-capacity low-lift pumping station equipped with vertical turbine pumps and variable frequency drives to elevate raw water into the rapid mixing chambers.
what: An industrial pump house building containing vertical turbine pumps, motors, suction piping manifold, and hydraulic surge protection vessels.
why: Lifts raw water from low river/intake elevation up to the higher gravitational hydraulic gradient required for gravity flow through treatment units.
how: Electric motors turn vertical pump shafts, drawing water from the wet pit and forcing it through discharge manifolds equipped with check valves and surge arrestors.
engineeringPurpose: Lifting raw water with variable flow control while protecting downstream pipelines against water hammer surge pressure.

components.what: Multi-stage vertical turbine pumps with submerged impellers and top-mounted electric motors.
components.why: Maintains prime automatically because impellers are constantly submerged in suction well.
components.how: Electric motor turns vertical drive shaft enclosed in column pipe, forcing water upward.

components.name: Variable Frequency Drive Control Panel
components.description: Electrical VFD panels modulating pump motor speeds based on inflow rates.
components.what: Solid-state electronic power inverter panels controlling motor frequency.
components.why: Adjusts pumping output dynamically without energy-wasting throttling valves.
components.how: Varying AC supply frequency (30-60 Hz) modifies motor rotational speed.

components.name: Hydraulic Surge Vessel & Discharge Main
components.description: Pressurized vessel protecting pipeline against water hammer transients.
components.what: Steel pressure vessel with elastomer bladder filled with compressed air.
components.why: Absorbs pressure spikes caused by sudden pump trips or valve closures.
components.how: Compressed air cushion contracts and expands to damp hydraulic shockwaves.

hotspots.label: Vertical Pump Motors

name: Coagulation Flash Mixer & Flocculation Basins
description: Rapid chemical dispersion basin followed by multi-stage gentle paddle flocculators where Alum/PAC coagulants destabilize colloidal particles to build settleable flocs.
what: A multi-stage chemical mixing unit comprising a high-speed flash mixer tank followed by a series of low-speed baffled paddle flocculator channels.
why: Raw water contains negatively charged colloidal particles (clay, organic matter) that naturally repel each other and will not settle. Coagulants neutralize charges so particles aggregate.
how: Coagulant chemical (Alum/PAC) is rapidly mixed in 30-60 seconds under high shear. Then water flows through 3 paddle stages with decreasing velocity gradients (G-values) to form heavy flocs.
engineeringPurpose: Charge neutralization of suspended colloidal particles followed by gentle agglomeration into heavy, settleable flocs.

parameters.name: Flash Mix Velocity Gradient (G)
parameters.description: High shear rate for rapid chemical dispersion

parameters.name: Flocculator G-Values
parameters.description: Tapered mixing velocity gradient across 3 stages

components.name: High-Speed Rapid Flash Mixer
components.description: Impeller mixing chamber dispersing coagulants within 30-60 seconds.
components.what: High-speed vertical turbine impeller chamber.
components.why: Ensures instant, uniform chemical distribution before hydrolysis reactions complete.
components.how: Motor rotates impeller at 300 RPM producing high shear intensity.

components.name: Tapered Slow Paddle Flocculators
components.description: Rotating mechanical paddles fostering particle collisions without shearing flocs.
components.what: Large horizontal or vertical wooden/fiberglass paddle wheels.
components.why: Provides gentle fluid motion to promote floc collisions without tearing flocs apart.
components.how: Variable speed motor drives turn paddle shafts slowly (2 to 6 RPM).
components.engineeringPurpose: Floc agglomeration via controlled fluid velocity gradients.

components.name: Coagulant Dosing Skid & Polymer Feed
components.description: Automated chemical pumps metering aluminum sulfate or polyaluminum chloride.
components.what: Duplex diaphragm metering pump skid with peristaltic dosing calibration columns.
components.why: Injects precise ppm chemical dosages matched to real-time raw water turbidity.
components.how: SCADA controls pump stroke length based on online turbidimeter feedback.

hotspots.label: Tapered Flocculator Paddles
hotspots.description: Slowly rotates (2-5 RPM) to agglomerate fine particles into heavy flocs.

name: High-Efficiency Clarifier & Sedimentation Basin
description: Circular or rectangular settling basin equipped with inclined tube settlers and a continuous bottom sludge scraper rake to remove heavy precipitated flocs.
what: A circular reinforced concrete settling tank with a central feed well, inclined tube settler modules, peripheral overflow launders, and a revolving bottom sludge scraper.
why: Removes 85-95% of suspended solids and chemical flocs by gravity settling before water reaches the rapid sand filters, extending filter run times.
how: Flocculated water enters central well at low velocity. Water travels outward radially. Flocs settle downward onto tank floor while clarified supernatant overflows peripheral V-notch weirs.
engineeringPurpose: Gravity clarification and solids removal under laminar settling regimes (low overflow rates).

components.why: Reduces vertical settling distance to a few centimeters, increasing effective settling capacity 4-fold.
components.how: Flocs drop onto lower tube surface and slide downward into sludge zone by gravity.

components.name: Center-Driven Rotating Sludge Scraper
components.description: Motorized scraper arm consolidating settled sludge into central hopper.

components.why: Prevents anaerobic sludge degradation and septic gas flotation.
components.how: Revolving squeegee blades sweep settled sludge into central bottom sump.

components.name: V-Notch Effluent Overflow Launders

name: Rapid Gravity Sand & Dual-Media Filter
description: Multi-bed filtration unit consisting of anthracite coal, silica sand, and gravel underdrains with automatic air/water backwash cleansing cycle.

why: Strains remaining micro-flocs, algae, Giardia cysts, and fine suspended particles to achieve drinking water turbidity < 0.1 NTU.
how: Water flows downward through media by gravity. Particles are trapped in pore spaces. When head loss increases, automated backwash reverses flow upward with air scour and water flush.
engineeringPurpose: Physical removal of sub-micron particulate matter and turbidity reduction prior to disinfection.

components.how: Larger particles trap in coarse top anthracite; fine turbidity traps in silica sand.
